headline: Pricing and Americas growth power a broad beat
summary_short: MSA Safety's Q2 FY2026 net sales rose to $503.3M, up 6.2% y/y (8.6% q/q), with diluted EPS of $2.23 up 40.3% y/y as operating income climbed 30.4% y/y to $112.0M.
summary_long: Net sales rose 6.2% y/y (3.2% organic): Americas +6.7% (4.5% organic) on industrial PPE and detection strength, offset by AFG-delayed fire-service orders; International +5.1% (0.3% organic) as ballistic-helmet demand offset a Middle East-driven detection decline. Gross margin expanded to 49.5% from 46.6% on price realization, productivity, and tariff refunds, partly offset by inflation. Operating income rose 30.4% y/y on higher gross profit and lower currency losses, partly offset by higher SG&A and restructuring. Tax rate fell to 22.6% from 24.1% on Pillar 2 benefits. Management reiterated mid-single-digit FY2026 organic growth guidance and $8-10M of pension contributions. Cash was $200.1M; MSA closed the ~$555M Autronica acquisition on July 9.

drivers.explanation: Americas sales +6.7% (4.5% organic) on double-digit industrial PPE and high-single-digit detection growth, offset by fire-service softness from delayed AFG funding; International +5.1% (0.3% organic) as European ballistic-helmet demand offset a Middle East-driven detection decline.
Margin rose to 49.5% from 46.6% on price realization, productivity and value-added engineering, plus favorable transactional FX and tariff refunds, partly offset by inflation.
Growth was primarily driven by higher gross profit and lower currency exchange losses, partially offset by higher SG&A and restructuring charges.
Reflects higher operating income and a lower effective tax rate (22.6% vs 24.1%), aided by benefits from finalizing initial Pillar 2 global minimum tax filings.

Management cited healthy backlog, a double-digit year-over-year order increase, and strong second-half demand pipeline (particularly U.S. fire service), while flagging continued tariff and Middle East geopolitical uncertainty.
